title: Renew a motor vehicle tradesperson certificate
summary: This page explains how to renew your motor vehicle tradesperson certificate, which can be done online or at a Service NSW Centre.
intro:
You'll receive a renewal notice for your motor vehicle tradesperson certificate a month prior to your certificate's expiry.

You can then apply for a 1, 3 or 5-year certificate, online.

In some instances, you'll need to visit a Service NSW Centre to renew your certificate.

Note: If your certificate expires, you are no longer authorised to carry out the type of repair work outlined on your certificate.

To find your certificate number and details, visit Verify NSW.
who_can_apply: You can renew online if you have your renewal number and certificate number.
You may need to visit a Service NSW Centre if you do not have your renewal number, have changed your name, or cannot confirm the online declaration.
If your name, address, or other details change, you must inform Service NSW within 14 days.
what_you_need: Renewal number (as shown on your renewal notice)

how_to_steps.text: Follow the prompts to renew your certificate.

more_info.text: If you did not renew on time but the licence is within 3 months from its expiry date you can apply to restore your certificate.
If your certificate has expired more than 3 months, you may need to apply for a new licence to be re-issued.

faqs.q: How do I renew my motor vehicle tradesperson certificate?
faqs.a: You can apply for a 1, 3, or 5-year certificate online. You will receive a renewal notice one month before your certificate expires, or you may need to visit a Service NSW Centre.

faqs.q: What happens if my certificate expires?
faqs.a: If your certificate expires, you are no longer authorised to carry out the type of repair work outlined on your certificate.

faqs.q: Where can I find my certificate number and details?
faqs.a: You can visit Verify NSW to find your certificate number and details.
